voyage.name: Palazzo Pubblico
voyage.content: This striking structure has functioned as Siena's City Hall for almost 800 years and is probably the building that most recognizably represents Siena. It contains (among many other things) the famous frescoes on good and bad government by Ambrogio Lorenzetti, frescoes by Simone Martini and Duccio, and access to the Torre del Mangia, from the top of which you can view a beautiful panorama of the Sienese countryside. T

voyage.name: Palazzo Piccolomini
voyage.content: One of the most popular sites on the Piazza del Campo, it was built in 1459 by the well-known architect Bernardo Rossellino, disciple of Leon Battista Alberti. This Florentine-style palazzo is home to the official archives of Siena.

voyage.name: Palazzo Sansedoni
voyage.content: Opposite the Palazzo Pubblico, it is another beautiful Gothic building on the Campo.

voyage.name: Fonte Gaia
voyage.content: The fountain sculpted in 1419 by the great Sienese sculptor, Jacopo della Quercia, is a focal point of the piazza. The remains of the original sculptures can be viewed in the loggia of the Palazzo Pubblico (see above), but the appearance of the fountain, composed of copies made in 1858, is not bad and remains a major sight in this city.

voyage.name: Duomo di Siena
voyage.price: The ticket options are confusing. The Opa Si Pass (€1 Nov-24 Dec €8, 18 Aug-27 Oct €15, €13 at other times) is valid for 3 days, and allows admission to the Duomo, including the Libreria Piccolomini and Crypt, the Baptistery, Museo dell'Opera and Facciatone. A €20 "all inclusive" pass will get you access to the Duomo and to the "Porta del Cielo", which provides great views of the interior of the church from up above, and views of the city from its roof. Otherwise, you can see details of costs for individual tickets here
voyage.hours: The open hours of the Cathedral, Library, Museum, Panorama, Crypt and Baptistery are generally the same, except that you may not enter the museum less than 1 hour before closing time. Complete opening hours information here; "Festive" means Sundays and church holidays. Exclusive of Sundays and holidays (festivi), everything opens at 10:30 and closes at 19:00 between 1 March and 2 November and at 17:30 between 3 November and 28 February, except that the closing hour is 18:00 between 26 December and 6 January
voyage.content: Siena's magnificent black and white Italian Romanesque cathedral includes the Libreria Piccolomini, with splendid frescoes by Pinturicchio, the lovely Baptistery (separate entrance and charge), and an attached museum (separate entrance and charge, see below). Also marvel at the inlaid floors; even as they are sometimes covered for protection, a section is always left visible. At the height of Siena's power it was dec

voyage.name: Museo dell'Opera del Duomo
voyage.alt: Museum of the Works of the Cathedral
voyage.price: Admission: €7, or see information on Opa Si Pass above
voyage.content: This museum includes the famous Maestà by Duccio and many other great works by Sienese masters. After you've seen all the art, you can also treat yourself to a beautiful panorama from Il Facciatone, the tower in this building. The view is about as good as the one from the Torre del Mangia in the Palazzo Pubblico but somewhat different, although if you are rushed for time, pick one tower to climb (either one).

voyage.name: Pinacoteca Nazionale di Siena
voyage.price: Regular admission: €4; reduction for students from the EU aged 18-25 and their docents: €2; free entry to children, and to everyone on the first Sunday of every month
voyage.content: The Pinacoteca is full of Sienese paintings from the city's Medieval heyday.

voyage.name: Palazzo Chigi-Saracini
voyage.content: This is another Gothic palazzo, or at least its façade remains Gothic, though the interior was modernized in the late 18th and early 19th centuries. The building since 1932 has housed housed the Accademia Chigiana, the city's conservatory of music. Quite a number of beautiful paintings are part of its collection, but the rooms that house the artwork are often used for classes and rehearsals or simply locked up when n

voyage.name: Palazzo Tolomei
voyage.content: This lovely palazzo was built between 1205 and 1212 by the Tolomei family when the area was outside of the city walls. Now, it is well within the walls and on the way from the Campo to Piazza Salimbeni.

voyage.name: Basilica Cateriniana San Domenico
voyage.hours: From March to October: 07:00-18:30, from November to February: 09:00-18:00
voyage.content: This large, austere Gothic basilica (usually simply called San Domenico) is not only dedicated to St. Catherine of Siena, along with St. Dominic, but was frequented by her and contains a period portrait of her by Andrea Vanni and relics including her head. It also features several other works by Sienese Gothic painters and impressively high vaulted ceilings. It is quite close to the long-distance bus stop, so if you

voyage.name: Basilica of San Francesco
voyage.content: This Romanesque church was turned into a Gothic one and contains some notable Gothic art, including a moving fresco of the Crucifixion by Pietro Lorenzetti and one of the Martyrdom of Five Franciscan Brothers by his brother, Ambrogio.

voyage.name: Birth House of St. Catherine of Siena
voyage.content: In this house lived the 14th-century mystic who is one of the principal patron saints of Italy. If you are a devotee, it is natural to combine a visit here with a visit to San Domenico, but even if you are not a devotee, if you have the time, you are likely to find your visit interesting.

voyage.name: Sant'Agostino
voyage.content: Built as a Gothic church, it was damaged by fire in 1747 and was renovated with some Baroque additions and further added to in the 19th century. However, the main draws for the lover of paintings are from well before the fire and include an Enthroned Madonna with Child and Saints by the 14th-century Ambrogio Lorenzetti and a Crucifixion by the 15th-16th-century Perugino.

voyage.name: Santa Maria dei Servi
voyage.content: This Romanesque church is much smaller than the huge edifices of the Duomo and San Domenico, but it contains some notable art including a Coronation of the Virgin and Saints by Bernardino Fungai, a Massacre of the Innocents attributed to Pietro Lorenzetti and collaborators and an Adoration of the Shepherds by Taddeo Di Bartolo.

voyage.name: Fontebranda
voyage.content: This medieval fountain is the oldest in Siena, built in its current form in 1246. It is the original, not a replica. Not surprisingly, it is somewhat worn and overgrown in places, but still impressive and beautiful, and would be a top sight in most other cities.

voyage.name: Santa Maria della Scala
voyage.content: This medieval hospital, now a museum, is chock-full of medieval art including altarpieces by Bartolommeo Bulgarini and frescoes by the Lorenzetti brothers and Simone Martini. Also part of the complex (no additional admission charge) is the Museo Archeologico Nazionale, which exhibits some important archeological finds from the area, plus items from public and private collections of antiquities that are mostly from Si

voyage.name: Palio Horse Race
voyage.content: A horse race like nowhere else, between the 17 contrade of Siena, is run in the Piazza del Campo on July 2 and August 16. All Sienese are affiliated with one of the contrade, to which a typical Sienese feels loyal with a strength perhaps surpassed only by their loyalty to their family. Since the 11th century, the Sienese have conducted festivals every year in which the contrade compete for renown (and in times gone b

voyage.name: Siena Jazz Festival
voyage.content: During summer.

voyage.name: Olive Oil
voyage.content: If you have a car then you can drive out to the Montestigliano Olive estate 12 km outside the walls, perched high on a hill surrounded by olive trees. You can taste and buy their single estate, extra virgin olive oil (as well as a few other goodies) to take with you or have shipped. There is also a lovely courtyard where you can sit and enjoy a glass of wine and admire the view.

voyage.name: Osteria Nonna Gina
voyage.content: Outside the Due Porte.

voyage.name: Osteria del Gatto
voyage.content: Not far from the above Nonna Gina. Menu will be in Italian but the waiters and the cooks will be available for a translation "on the fly". Fish is served one week a month. If you happen to be there in that week, don't miss the "Tonno alla Mediterranea" (tuna fish in the Mediterranean way).

voyage.name: Trattoria la Torre
voyage.content: This is also an excellent restaurant, in the contrada of the same name.

voyage.name: Osteria Sotto le Fonti
voyage.content: Restaurant off the beaten path, with owners who serve you personally; the waitress speaks fluently English & German (very rare in Italy) and knows how to recommend you wine, as she is also a wine tour guide. Is a pleasant walk downhill shortly outside the gates of the city, allowing you to look up at the top of the Duomo.

voyage.name: Bar Pasticceria Nannini
voyage.content: A bakery and cafe with an excellent selection of Tuscan pastries: Ricciarelli, Cavalucci, Cantucci, Panforte, etc. The ingredients of same are prominently displayed in most cases, making Nannini a very attractive option for the travelling vegan.

voyage.name: Antica Osteria da Divo
voyage.content: Has a splendid atmosphere in a medieval undercroft environment and excellent Italian cuisine served in a decorative haute style.

voyage.name: Ristorante Sansedoni in Birreria
voyage.content: Best priced drinks and food in Il Campo. Sit outside at a table in the central Piazza.

voyage.name: Barone Rosso
voyage.content: Great live music, but a bit on the seedy side.

voyage.name: The Walkabout Pub
voyage.content: Cool pub with Australian ambiance doing cool music.

voyage.name: Siena Colleverde
voyage.content: About 3 km east from the city centre and up the hill from the rail station. It is quite a large campsite and has all the facilities and a swimming pool. As of 2012, you can rent cabins with toilet/shower for 2/3/4/5 persons (€65/80/105/115 per night, maybe cheaper when booked through traveling sites).

voyage.name: Montagnola
voyage.content: Beyond the small village of Sovicille about 12 km from Siena with regular bus connections. It's a decent site with basic facilities but quite friendly and helpful staff.

voyage.name: Agriturismo Monaciano
voyage.address: Tenuta di Monaciano, Ponte a Bozzone
voyage.content: Tuscany self catering accommodations in the Chianti hills 7 km from Siena with swimming pool, ping-pong and a romantic park. Monaciano has many farmhouses that may comfortably accommodate large families or large groups of friends.

voyage.name: Santuario S. Caterina
voyage.content: Run by a nunnery, this modest hotel near the Basilica di S. Domenico provides sanctuary to weary travellers. Curfew is 23:00.

voyage.name: La Villa di STR
voyage.content: 3-star hotel that offers free shuttle service for the Spa San Giovanni Rapolano Terme.

voyage.name: Albergo Bernini
voyage.content: Via della Sapienza n°15 (just down the street from San Domenico) (use Italian or simple English if you email) - dated but clean rooms in a tiny, centrally-located inn. A truly friendly older couple owns and runs it, and lives on the property (they leave their door open often). The great thing is the view of Siena - spectacular, as you look across the unobstructed valley and almost down at the Piazza del Campo and Duo

voyage.name: Piccolo Hotel Etruria
voyage.content: Via Donzelle 3. You can't beat the location; it's just a couple of steps up from the Campo. Clean, renovated, has a nice common room with a small balcony right over Banchi di Sotto - the final leg of the route towards the Campo taken by the constant parades of the contrada which won the latest palio (these last for a few weekends after the event, and can mean a group of thoroughly drunk stragglers accompanied by cost

voyage.name: NH Excelsior
voyage.content: Piazza La Lizza. Situated inside the walls, the NH Excelsior is elegant and pleasant, and has easy access to the city’s main attractions. The hotel, which has been completely refurbished, has 129 rooms all of which offer comfort and a modern design.

voyage.name: The Hotel Minerva
voyage.content: Via Garibaldi, 72, inside the walls of Siena. There are 59 bedrooms with bathrooms, phone, TV, safe deposit box, air conditioning, fridge-bar, laundry service, fast internet facility. The bedrooms have a view of old Siena. A meeting room is available. Garage. Ten minutes' walk from Piazza del Campo. 500 m from the railway station.

voyage.name: Le Meridiane
voyage.content: Le Meridiane is across the valley from the city centre and provides a lovely view of Siena, which can be reached by bus, by taxi or (during daylight and with good shoes) by foot. Several types of unit are available for a range of prices. A small kitchen is provided, and parking is available.

voyage.name: Borgo Grondaie
voyage.content: A typical farmhouse hotel with swimming pool. It offers a selection of studio apartments and en-suite rooms in a country and friendly atmosphere.

voyage.name: Chiostro del Carmine
voyage.content: 4-star hotel in historical residence, Siena centre. Rooms from €99.

voyage.name: Montaperti Hotel
voyage.content: About 7 km east of Siena, close to the SS73 highway. Situated in the middle of a rural landscape next to a vineyard and a small village. Convenient only if you have access to a car, in which case, it's easy to get to and from Siena.

voyage.name: Villa Agostoli
voyage.content: Beautiful holiday house pet friendly with pool and vacation rental apartments near Siena.

voyage.name: Hotel Italia
voyage.address: Viale Camillo Benso Conte di Cavour, 67
voyage.content: 3-star hotel. The hotel has a Love Room for romantic moments.

voyage.name: Hotel Garden
voyage.content: 4-stars hotel with restaurant, outdoor pool and panoramic terrace. With Hotel Italia and Villa Agostoli, the Hotel Garden is one of the hotels in Siena of the company Siena Inns.

voyage.name: Borgo Scopeto Relais
voyage.content: Beautiful 4-star hotel and restaurant immersed in vineyards and olive groves of the Tuscan countryside 12 km from Siena. Also does weddings and meetings.

voyage.name: Campo Regio Relais
voyage.content: A bed and breakfast-style hotel, renovated in 2005, in the historical centre of Siena, with amazing view onto the old town.

voyage.name: Residence "Villa Il Borghetto"
voyage.content: Splendid aristocratic residence originating in the early 1600s, in the countryside, ten minutes' drive from the historical centre of Siena. It incorporates eight spacious apartments, which may host up to seven persons. It is complemented by the Dependence, a holiday home to the same standard. Each of the eight spacious apartments is a synthesis of comfort, elegant style, traditional taste and modern functionality.
